claim: pyright reportAttributeAccessIssue x299: "Cannot access attribute X for class <Mixin>*" across downloader/download/player/version/search/media_info
rationale: Architectural, not a defect. STANDARDS.md section 2.2 documents mixin composition: SnatchApp in snatch/app.py inherits from 7 mixins, and each mixin legitimately reads attributes its siblings define. Pyright type-checks each mixin in isolation and cannot see the composed class, so every cross-mixin attribute read is reported. 299 of pyright's 302 reportAttributeAccessIssue findings are this shape. The remaining 3 are module-attribute reads and are logged separately.

claim: ruff S310 x4 / bandit B310 x3 / semgrep dynamic-urllib-use-detected x3: urllib.request.urlopen may allow file:// or custom schemes (downloader.py:285,287; version.py:78,243)
rationale: Every one of the three call sites is scheme-constrained before the open. downloader.py:283 guards with thumbnail_url.startswith("https://"). version.py:76 opens the module constant YTDLP_RELEASE_API, which is not dynamic at all. version.py:236 raises ValueError("refusing a download that is not HTTPS") on anything not starting https://, two lines above the Request. No file:// or custom scheme can reach any of the three.

claim: ruff S603 x10 and semgrep dangerous-subprocess-use-tainted-env-args (player.py:140): subprocess call with untrusted input
rationale: All ten sites already carry the hardening the rule asks you to confirm, per CLAUDE.md's mandatory subprocess rules. Every call uses the argv list form, never shell=True and never sh -c. Every site taking a URL or path emits the "--" separator before it: downloader.py:190, downloader.py:635, player.py:131, media_info.py:109, search.py:294, platform_utils.py:260 and 262. Every URL is validated by DownloaderMixin._is_valid_url (snatch/downloader.py:74, http/https only) at downloader.py:156,584,792, player.py:78 and download.py:401. Every call passes an explicit timeout.

claim: semgrep insecure-file-permissions (version.py:256): os.chmod(tmp_path, 0o700) is widely permissive
rationale: 0o700 is owner-only rwx, which is the minimum for a file that must then be executed. The target is the freshly downloaded yt-dlp binary in a mkstemp file, probed by _probe_version at version.py:257 before os.replace promotes it. Group and other have no access at all. The rule's own remedy (narrow the mode) is already what the code does; there is no narrower mode that still permits execution by the owner.

claim: pyright reportPossiblyUnbound (downloader.py:289-291 Image/ImageTk), reportOptionalIterable (downloader.py:93, 651), reportOptionalMemberAccess (downloader.py:697), and 3 module-attribute reads (PIL.Image.LANCZOS, sys._MEIPASS, os.startfile)
rationale: Each is guarded in a way pyright cannot follow. Image/ImageTk are conditionally imported and every use sits behind the HAS_PIL flag (downloader.py:283) that the same import sets — the feature-detection pattern STANDARDS.md section 8.4 prescribes. _cached_runtimes is None only until _ensure_runtime_cache() runs, called at downloader.py:88, three lines above the iteration. download_process.stdout is non-None because the Popen at downloader.py:637 passes stdout=subprocess.PIPE. PIL.Image.LANCZOS exists at runtime and is a stub gap. sys._MEIPASS exists only under PyInstaller and is read defensively. os.startfile is Windows-only, guarded by is_windows() at platform_utils.py:255 and already carrying an explicit noqa.

"datas" is PyInstaller's own API keyword, not English. Analysis(datas=[...]) and COLLECT(...) take it by that exact spelling; renaming it would break the spec file. The ROADMAP.md:593 occurrence is prose quoting the same keyword. This is a standing false positive for any project shipping a .spec file.

claim: vulture: unused variable args (widgets.py:103, 100% confidence); unused attributes is_processing_queue and is_playlist (app.py:73,78 and downloader.py:769,824,831,851,870); unused variable HAS_MPV (__init__.py:11)
rationale: widgets.py:103 _on_var_change(self, *args) is a tkinter trace-callback signature — Tk passes three positional arguments to a write trace, so *args is required by the protocol and cannot be removed. is_processing_queue and is_playlist are cross-file instance attributes: app.py initialises them and downloader.py reads and writes them at the five lines vulture lists, which vulture cannot correlate because it analyses each file's attribute names in isolation. HAS_MPV is a package-level feature flag exported from snatch/__init__.py and consumed by other modules; CLAUDE.md names it as one of the three detected-at-import flags.

claim: ruff E501 x79: line too long (> 88 characters) across snatch/
rationale: 88 is ruff's default and is not this project's declared limit. STANDARDS.md section 10.1 states "PEP 8 style with 100-char line limit (soft)". Re-run at the declared limit, ruff check --select E501 --line-length 100 reports 21, not 79 — so 58 of the 79 are the tool disagreeing with the project's own standard rather than a breach of it. The remaining 21 are real but soft by the standard's own wording. The underlying gap is that no pyproject.toml carries the 100 so the declared limit is enforced by nothing; that is filed as a roadmap item rather than dismissed here.

claim: ruff S110 x6: try-except-pass, consider logging the exception (app.py:161, downloader.py:698,777, player.py:239,246, download.py:392)
rationale: All six are best-effort teardown or optional-feature paths where there is no action a handler could take. app.py:161 is a cosmetic window-icon load. downloader.py:698 closes a stdout pipe inside a finally block, which CLAUDE.md mandates ("Close subprocess pipes in finally blocks"); a failure to close leaves nothing to do. downloader.py:777 and player.py:239,246 are process termination and socket unlink during cancel/close. download.py:392 registers an optional drag-and-drop target behind the HAS_DND flag. Suppressing these individually is not proposed; the real gap is that the app has no logging path at all, which is filed as a roadmap item rather than dismissed.

claim: ruff S607 x2: starting a process with a partial executable path (platform_utils.py:260, 262 — "open" and "xdg-open"); ruff S101 x2: use of assert (scripts/verify_platform_utils.py:31,33)
rationale: S607: xdg-open and open have no fixed absolute path across distributions and macOS releases, so PATH resolution is the documented way to invoke them; hardcoding /usr/bin/xdg-open breaks on distributions that ship it elsewhere. Exploiting this needs an already-compromised PATH, at which point the app is not the boundary. S101: verify_platform_utils.py is the project's build-time smoke check, run by build-linux.sh:20, build-windows.sh:20, build-macos.sh:22 and local-ci.sh:68 — assert is the whole mechanism by which it fails a build, and S101's rationale (asserts are stripped under python -O) does not apply to a script the build invokes directly.

claim: ruff F401 x2: tkinterdnd2.DND_TEXT and tkinterdnd2.TkinterDnD imported but unused (snatch/__init__.py:6); consider importlib.util.find_spec
rationale: The import IS the probe. snatch/__init__.py:5-9 is the feature-detection pattern STANDARDS.md section 8.4 prescribes: try the import, set HAS_DND from whether it succeeded. The names are deliberately not re-exported — snatch/__main__.py:8 and snatch/tabs/download.py:388 import TkinterDnD and DND_TEXT directly from the package at their point of use. Ruff's suggested find_spec is weaker here, not equivalent: tkinterdnd2 can be installed and still fail at import time when its bundled Tcl library is missing, which find_spec reports as present. Rewriting it would turn a working probe into one that lies on exactly the machines the flag exists for.

claim: zizmor cache-poisoning x3 on .github/workflows/ci.yml: the three build jobs pass `cache:` to actions/setup-python in a workflow that also publishes on a v* tag.
rationale: Mitigated in a form the tool cannot evaluate, not dismissed. SNAT-0047 made the key conditional: `cache: ${{ !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') && 'pip' || '' }}`, so a tag build -- the run whose artifacts are attached to the Release -- passes an empty value and does no caching. zizmor's audit fires on the presence of a `cache:` key alongside a publishing trigger and does not evaluate the expression, so it reports the same three regardless. Verified by executing the real workflow under act with both refs: with refs/heads/main the log carries "Cache restored from key" and two "Cache Size" lines; with refs/tags/v9.9.9 there is no cache restore or save at all. Re-check this if the expression is edited -- the first attempt, `startsWith(...) && '' || 'pip'`, was a no-op that always evaluated to 'pip' (GitHub's A && B || C is a ternary only while B is truthy), and zizmor's unsound-ternary audit is what caught it.
